newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end end lower on U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end end lower on U.S. rate fears.

text.p: Swiss shares closed sharply lower on Monday, loosing more than two percent in the blue-chip SMI index as fears of rising interest rates in the United States and possibly Germany put pressure on prices, dealers said.
Wall Street's lower start also depressed market sentiment, one dealer said.

European financial markets were worried by speculation the U.S. Federal Reserve would have to raise interest rates at its next policy-making meeting on August 19 and uncertainty surrounding the German central bank's next move.
The Swiss Market Index (SMI) lost 2.16 percent or 127.2 points to close at 5,771.0.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) dropped 1.78 percent or 66.84 points to 3,685.82 points.
Trading volume was 2.13 billion Swiss francs, dealers said.
Volume leader Novartis dropped 74 francs to close at 2,353.
Oerlikon-Buehrle lost three francs to 151, suffering from a public rift between the board and management of division bally over wthwesaidr the shoes and fashion division should go public.
ABB, due to report first-halt figures on Thursday, was 14 francs lower and closed at 2,135 francs.

Bearer shares of UBS declined 16 francs to 1,668 in spite of speculative buying. The bank is due to release its half-year figures around 0730 local/0530 GMT Tuesday. Analysts expect net profit to jump between nearly 50 and 70 percent.
CS Group lost 7.25 percent to close at 196.75.
Registered shares of SBC were nine francs lower at 400.
Insurers also lost ground with Winterthur falling 18 francs to 1.469 and Zurich dropping 13 francs to 603.
